Interface HWDiskStore

All Known Implementing Classes:
AbstractHWDiskStore, AixHWDiskStore, DragonFlyBsdHWDiskStore, FreeBsdHWDiskStore, LinuxHWDiskStore, LinuxHWDiskStoreNF, MacHWDiskStore, NetBsdHWDiskStore, OpenBsdHWDiskStore, SolarisHWDiskStore, WindowsHWDiskStore
@PublicApi @ThreadSafe public interface HWDiskStore
A storage mechanism where data are recorded by various electronic, magnetic, optical, or mechanical changes to a surface layer of one or more rotating disks or or flash storage such as a removable or solid state drive. In constrast to a File System, defining the way an Operating system uses the storage, the Disk Store represents the hardware which a FileSystem uses for its File Stores.

Each disk store contains a list of HWPartition objects. Partitions that are mounted have a HWPartition.getMountPoint() value that can be correlated with OSFileStore.getMount() to link hardware partitions to their corresponding file stores.

Example: finding the disk store and partition for a given file path: 

String filePath = "/home/user/data.txt";
for (HWDiskStore disk : hal.getDiskStores()) {
    for (HWPartition part : disk.getPartitions()) {
        if (!part.getMountPoint().isEmpty() && filePath.startsWith(part.getMountPoint())) {
            System.out.printf("File is on disk %s, partition %s%n", disk.getName(), part.getName());
        }
    }
}
Thread safe for the designed use of retrieving the most recent data. Users should be aware that the updateAttributes() method may update attributes, including the time stamp, and should externally synchronize such usage to ensure consistent calculations.

    • getDiskType

      default String getDiskType()
      The type of the disk's media.

      Determined on Linux from the device's removable and queue/rotational sysfs attributes, on macOS from the IOKit registry's Removable property and Medium Type, and on Windows from the storage driver's removable-media flag, bus type and seek penalty, falling back to MSFT_PhysicalDisk's MediaType and SpindleSpeed, and on FreeBSD from the rotationrate the drive reports to geom. Other platforms always report Unknown.

      Virtual is reported only for a Linux device-mapper device, a macOS APFS container or disk image, and a Windows file-backed virtual or Storage Spaces disk. A hypervisor's disk that the guest sees as an ordinary device is reported by its media technology, not as Virtual. Whether a disk duplicates the capacity and I/O of another entry in the list is reported by getBackingStores(), not by this type.

      Returns:
      one of SSD, HDD, Removable, Virtual, or Unknown where the type could not be determined, which includes a disk whose driver does not report it

    • getBackingStores

      default Optional<List<String>> getBackingStores()
      The stores this disk is built on, when it is a layer over other storage rather than a device in its own right.

      A layered disk is listed alongside the stores it is built on, so its capacity and I/O statistics duplicate theirs. This is the case for a device-mapper (LVM, LUKS, multipath) or md RAID device on Linux, an APFS container or a disk image on macOS, and a Storage Spaces or file-backed virtual disk on Windows.

      An empty Optional means the backing stores are not reported, either because the platform does not report them or because they could not be read, and says nothing about whether the disk is layered. A present but empty list means the disk is not built on anything OSHI can see. Summing the I/O of only the disks whose result is present and empty therefore counts each transfer once, provided every disk's result is present and every store it names is itself listed. Windows does not list the physical disks of a Storage Spaces pool, so there the Storage Spaces disk is the only entry carrying their transfers.

      Backing stores are reported on Linux, from each block device's sysfs slaves directory; on macOS, from the IOKit registry; and on Windows 8 and Server 2012 or later, from the Storage namespace of WMI. Other platforms return an empty Optional.

      Each entry is a HWDiskStore.StoreKind prefix followed by a name that matches a getter on the corresponding class:

      Backing store entries
      Kind Name matches Examples
      HWDiskStore.StoreKind.DISK getName() disk:/dev/sda, disk:\\.\PHYSICALDRIVE1
      HWDiskStore.StoreKind.PARTITION HWPartition.getIdentification() partition:/dev/sda2, partition:disk0s2
      HWDiskStore.StoreKind.FILE OSFileStore.getMount() of the file store holding the backing file file:/System/Volumes/Data, file:C:\
      An entry may name a store that is not in the current list, such as a network file store when only local file stores were requested.
      Returns:
      An Optional containing the stores this disk is built on, sorted, which is an empty list for a disk that is not layered; or empty if the backing stores are not reported.

    • updateAttributes

      boolean updateAttributes()
      Make a best effort to update all the statistics about the drive without needing to recreate the drive list. This method provides for more frequent periodic updates of individual drive statistics but may be less efficient to use if updating all drives. It will not detect if a removable drive has been removed and replaced by a different drive in between method calls.
      Returns:
      True if the update was (probably) successful, false if the disk was not found
